title: Caste, Tribal and Peasant Movements

cards.b: Reformers were often upper caste. Alongside them rose movements of the oppressed, tribes and peasants. UPSC asks for names, places, years and the colonial causes.

Colonial land revenue, forest laws, moneylenders and outsiders (dikus) hurt peasants and tribes. Missionaries and English education opened new ideas to lower castes. The state’s census (from 1871 to 1881) also hardened caste identity.

cards.h: Caste movements: the south and west
cards.b:
• Jotirao Phule: Gulamgiri (1873); Satyashodhak Samaj; first girls’ school at Pune, 1848 with Savitribai.
  • Self-Respect Movement (1925), E. V. Ramasamy Periyar.
  • SNDP (1903), Sree Narayana Guru, Kerala: “One caste, one religion, one God”.
  • Justice Party (1916) in Madras.
  • Vaikom Satyagraha (1924 to 25) for temple-road entry.

B. R. Ambedkar: Mahad Satyagraha (1927) for water; burnt the Manusmriti; Kalaram temple entry (Nashik 1930); Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924); Mooknayak (1920). He argued for separate electorates at the Round Table Conferences. The Poona Pact (1932) with Gandhi gave reserved seats within the general electorate (148 in provincial councils).

Gandhi started the Harijan and the All India Harijan Sangh (1932).

• Santhal Hul (1855 to 56): Sido and Kanhu, Rajmahal hills.
  • Munda Ulgulan (1899 to 1900): Birsa Munda, Chotanagpur.
  • Kol revolt (1831 to 32); Khasi (Tirut Singh, 1829 to 33); Bhil; Rampa (Alluri Sitarama Raju, 1922 to 24).
  • Chuar, Ho and Kherwar revolts.
Causes: loss of land, forest laws (Indian Forest Act 1865, 1878), outsiders and money lenders. Birsa Munda’s movement led to the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908.

• Indigo Revolt (1859 to 60, Bengal), Digambar and Bishnu Biswas; supported by Neel Darpan (Dinabandhu Mitra); Harish Chandra Mukherjee wrote in the Hindoo Patriot.
  • Pabna agrarian leagues (1873 to 76).
  • Deccan Riots (1875): against moneylenders; Deccan Agriculturists Relief Act 1879.
  • Moplah rebellions, Malabar (1836 to 1921).

• Champaran (1917), Gandhi’s first satyagraha in India.
  • Kheda (1918) and Bardoli (1928, Sardar Patel).
  • Eka Movement (UP, 1921), Kisan Sabha (Baba Ramchandra; UP Kisan Sabha 1918).
  • All India Kisan Sabha (1936, Lucknow), Swami Sahajanand Saraswati president.
  • Tebhaga (1946 to 47, Bengal) and Telangana (1946 to 51) risings.

Eric Hobsbawm called such movements “primitive rebellion”. Ranajit Guha and the Subaltern Studies group (Elementary Aspects of Peasant Insurgency, 1983) argue peasants had their own politics, separate from the elite. Critics say the school underplays Congress mobilisation and class differences among peasants.

The Fifth and Sixth Schedules, the PESA Act 1996 and the Forest Rights Act 2006 trace tribal anxieties to these revolts. Land reforms, minimum support price and the 2020 farm law protests tie to the peasant past. Birsa Munda’s birth anniversary (15 November) is celebrated as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas since 2021.

• “Tribal movements in colonial India had different causes from peasant movements. Discuss.”
  • “Compare Phule and Ambedkar on caste.”
  • Prelims tip: leader–place pairs (Birsa–Chotanagpur, Sido-Kanhu–Santhal Parganas) and years of the Poona Pact (1932), All India Kisan Sabha (1936).
